title: Differential compatibility of normalized Hom degree maps
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:A\to B$ a ring homomorphism, and $\mathcal M_A,\mathcal M_B$ the module-sheaf categories on the one-object bottom-topology site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F:\mathcal M_A\to\mathcal M_B$ be additive, with equalities $h_M:F(M)=\operatorname{changeOfRings}_{\varphi}(M)$ and $F(a)=h_M\circ\operatorname{changeOfRingsHom}_{\varphi}(a)\circ h_N^{-1}$ for every morphism $a:M\to N$, where composition is written in diagrammatic order [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $F^\bullet$ be termwise extension, $H_A,H_B$ the shared Hom complexes with their chosen product projections into internal Homs [def-pur-hom-complex, def-pur-sheaf-hom], and let $\operatorname{pure}_M(b,x)$ and $\operatorname{ev}_p$ denote the transported pure tensor and identity-slice evaluation [def-pc-ring-hom-extension-shared-definitions]. For arbitrary cochain complexes $P,Q$ in $\mathcal M_A$, suppose morphisms $t_n:F(H_A(P,Q)^n)\to H_B(F^\bullet P,F^\bullet Q)^n$ are supplied for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, satisfying $\operatorname{ev}_p(t_n(\operatorname{pure}_{H_A(P,Q)^n}(b,f)))(\operatorname{pure}_{P^p}(c,x))=\operatorname{pure}_{Q^{p+n}}(bc,\operatorname{ev}_p(f)(x))$ for every $n,p\in\mathbf Z$, site object $U$, $b,c\in B$, $f\in H_A(P,Q)^n(U)$ and $x\in P^p(U)$. Then for all $n,m\in\mathbf Z$, $t_n\circ d_{H_B}^{n,m}=d_{F^\bullet H_A}^{n,m}\circ t_m$, in diagrammatic composition order. This asserts compatibility of the supplied maps, not their existence.

proof.text: Verify the chain identity after every target product projection and on pure tensors. The given equality for F.map identifies extension of the differentials with their ordinary scalar-extension maps. In adjacent degrees the two contributions on both sides are bc tensor d_Q(f_p(x)) and minus (-1)^n bc tensor f_{p+1}(d_P(x)); additivity gives equality of their difference. In other degrees both differentials are zero. Pure tensors generate scalar extension on this bottom-topology site, and equality of product coordinates implies equality of the degree maps. This proves differential compatibility of the supplied normalized maps; no new maps are chosen.
